newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DAX index chases Dow to record highs.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DAX index chases Dow to record highs.

text.p: The German share market opened in bullish form on Tuesday, powered by record overnight gains in the U.S. and Japan and well-received results from top companies.
The DAX set a new high in early trade of 3,584.56 points, fifty points above its old record of 3,533.56, before easing back to trade at 3,570.26, up 41.48 points, or 1.2 percent.
Modest trading volumes, however, meant shares failed to sustain an early momentum which pushed the IBIS DAX of electronic trade over 3,600 points for the first time ever in pre-bourse dealings.
Nonetheless, the mood on the floor was optimistic.
"All the news has been positive today," said a Frankfurt dealer. "Wall Street was good, the Nikkei was better and we are simply keeping up."
Heading the field was diversified energy group Veba, boosted by a first quarter earnings report that dealers said was significatly above expectations.
Sportswear firm Adidas was also among the morning's outperformers after reporting a 33 percent rise in first quarter net profit, although its advance ebbed as trading continued.
Veba's shares topped turnover volumes in early trade as they rose 3.40 marks, or 3.9 percent to 93.60 marks.

"It looks like Veba will be the stock of the day," said one dealer. Veba said its first quarter net profit after minorities rose seven percent to 486 million marks while pre-tax profit rose 6.8 percent to 1.08 billion marks.
Adidas was up 2.50 marks, or 1.4 percent, at 183 marks in bourse trade, off an early high of 186.75 marks.
Other corporate news expected today includes a possible dividend announcement from airline Lufthansa AG and news from Hoechst AG's shareholder meeting.
